children: shares fell more than 4% Thursday as investors reacted to plans for as much as $3.5 billion from a convertible debt sale alongside a program to issue up to 35 million Class A shares.

The artificial-intelligence cloud provider is seeking $3 billion through convertible senior notes due in 2033. Buyers could purchase another $500 million, taking the potential debt offering to $3.5 billion.

CoreWeave also entered an equity distribution agreement covering as many as 35 million shares through several financial institutions. Proceeds from the note transaction are slated for capped-call transactions and general corporate purposes.

The financing push comes as CoreWeave carries large spending needs. The company expects 2026 capital expenditures of $35 billion to $39 billion, while its second-quarter backlog reached $104.2 billion and new customer commitments exceeded $25 billion early in the third quarter.

Competition adds another consideration for investors. Crux AI, backed by Google and Blackstone, has secured $22 billion in bank financing for data centers built around Google's Tensor Processing Units as CoreWeave expands its AI infrastructure business.

title: CoreWeave Shares Sink on $3 Billion Convertible Notes
